# Security verdict, #323 round 1 at 134b0109a468024892eccf161392e1272d3bfa58: pass

Static review of picture.rs, community/directory.rs and core/directory.rs, in a detached worktree. CI 5/5 SUCCESS at this head.

## Can the new grouping hide a real duplicate holder, letting two seats both act on one PR?
No authority changes. `duplicate_holders` only drives ADVICE: the Next actions, the directory JSON, the open-work read gate and the W-ONE-HOLDER warning. Assignment was already allowed with a warning, and still is. Who can act on a role or instance is decided elsewhere: E-RS-ROLE-HOLDERS routing and `pij output`'s writer check are unchanged in this diff. So hiding a duplicate here could at worst mean a missed warning, never a grant.
- Grouping is by exact `instance` (with '' as the bare role). A group is flagged when it contains any seat other than its first, so two distinct seats on the same holding are always flagged, and a seat holding the same instance twice is not. The case that is no longer flagged is one seat on the bare role plus another seat on `<role>/<n>`. They are different holdings with different routing addresses, so they are not one PR held twice. Whether that mix should warn is a policy question for the reviewer, not a security one.

## Can the release advice ever target the wrong seat?
No. Each action is built from one group, whose rows all share an instance. Every command is `pij directory release <address(row)> <row.seat>`, using that row's own role/instance and seat, and filtered with `row.seat != kept.seat`. So the kept seat is never targeted, and a release for /322 cannot name /320. When two or more holders have open work, it prints no commands, as before. Commands pass `printable(row)`, and every word goes through the existing `command()` quoting, unchanged.

No secrets, lockfile or `.npmrc` changes.
